answer: Each agent must accumulate a time-locked stake before it can submit work, and rewards are released only after independent peers verify its output. A prism of checks lets peers compare results without trusting one identity, while a public beacon records stake age and challenge outcomes. Sybils can still be created, but each needs separate capital held at risk; splitting one stake across many names does not multiply voting weight. The velvet cost is delayed access and funds lost to slashing when fabricated work fails review.
